title: Man polishing powder horn outside Lexington church prompts bizarre police response
author: Darin Zullo
bullets: Lexington police responded to a report of a man with a gun outside Grace Chapel, prompting a lockdown.
The man was polishing a historical powder horn, leading to the misunderstanding; he was not a threat.
The police response included multiple cruisers and road closures, but no public danger was present.

title: Longtime sports analyst Rob Parker not sold that Red Sox will make playoffs
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Sports analyst Rob Parker doubts Red Sox can sustain current success to secure a playoff spot in 2026.
Red Sox hold the second A.L. wild-card spot with a 64-52 record and a 96% playoff likelihood per FanGraphs.
Parker maintains skepticism despite Red Sox's historic winning streak and strong statistical playoff chances.

title: Chad Tracy ‘hopeful’ Wilyer Abreu is back in Red Sox lineup Sunday
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: Wilyer Abreu was scratched from the Red Sox lineup Saturday due to swelling after being hit in the leg Friday.
Chad Tracy is hopeful Abreu will return for Sunday's game against the Athletics following treatment for his minor injury.
Abreu has contributed significantly this season, with 20 home runs, 62 RBIs, and a .793 OPS for the Red Sox.

title: Red Sox’ latest winning streak ends at 9 games after loss to Athletics
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: The Boston Red Sox lost 7-3 to the Athletics, ending their nine-game winning streak.
Red Sox out-hit the Athletics 10-8 but left 12 runners on base and struck out 15 times.
Pitcher Jake Bennett allowed four earned runs over 5.1 innings; Boston's bullpen struggled further.

title: Here’s why Gillette Stadium is swapping out its turf surface again so soon after the World Cup
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Gillette Stadium is replacing its turf again due to an NFL rule requiring compliance with specific testing protocols.
The current turf at Gillette Stadium doesn't meet NFL laboratory testing standards because it lacks an 'E-layer'.
A previous surface, used by the Patriots and Revolution in 2025, will replace the current non-compliant turf.

title: 4 takeaways from the Revolution’s loss vs. Houston Dynamo
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: New England Revolution lost 2-0 to Houston Dynamo at Gillette Stadium, with goals from Guilherme and Agustin Resch.
Revolution's new signing Jack Harrison made his debut, entering in the 55th minute, but couldn't impact the outcome.
Houston effectively countered New England's attacks, securing the win with a second goal from Resch in the 63rd minute.

title: Here’s the latest injury updates on Roman Anthony, Adley Rutschman
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: Roman Anthony uses a pitching machine to practice with higher velocities as he recovers from a wrist injury.
Adley Rutschman started a rehab stint, playing five innings with the Worcester Red Sox, improving his fitness.
Boston Red Sox maintain a 9-game winning streak, set to strengthen lineup with Rutschman and Anthony's returns.

title: New on Netflix and more: Top streaming picks for August 2026
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: Netflix highlights for August include 'Clueless,' 'Eighth Grade,' and 'Something’s Gotta Give.'
Paramount+ features 'Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender,' continuing the hit Nickelodeon series.
Boston.com staff recommend shows like 'Ted Lasso' on Apple TV and 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' on Paramount+.

title: An 8-foot Bigfoot was spotted in Connecticut last month. It’s far from New England’s first.
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Kevin Klimas reported an eight-foot Bigfoot sighting in Voluntown, Connecticut, on July 5, avoiding a collision with it.
The Bigfoot Field Researchers Organization verified 126 sightings in New England since 1994, including Klimas's recent sighting.
Boston University professor Eva Garrett states there's no scientific evidence for Bigfoot, comparing it to ancient giant ape myths.

title: I will miss my friend Margo, who told me to grieve, but not too much
author: Meredith Goldstein
bullets: Meredith Goldstein recounts her friendship with Margo Howard, daughter of Ann Landers, and her impact on dealing with grief.
Margo Howard, who died last month at 86, was known for her practical, sometimes sarcastic, advice as a columnist.
Margo encouraged Goldstein to balance grieving with finding new happiness, leaving a lasting influence on her friend.
